title: AutoInt: Automatic Feature Interaction Learning via Self-Attentive Neural Networks
grouping: No containers. The field embeddings sit at the left (a stack at top-left, the query field e_m alone at bottom-left); three blue arrows fan out to the value stack (top right), the key stack (middle) and the query box (bottom). Curly braces gather keys with the query into the attention weights, and values with weights into the output on the far right.
shapes_depth: Flat filled rectangles with thin outlines, no shadows. Field embeddings are three offset light-blue cards (e_1 … e_M, a dot between them for omitted fields); keys are grey offset cards, values gold offset cards, the query a single peach box. The attention weights alpha_m^(h) are a vertical column of small olive squares printed with example numbers (0.1, 0.8, …, 0.02). The output e~_m^(h) is a grey square. Projection arrows are blue and labelled W_Value^(h), W_Key^(h), W_Query^(h) in italic math.
proposed_highlight: The whole figure is the proposed interacting layer; the attention weights are the one element drawn with example values, in a darker olive than the rest.
lesson: Show attention over feature fields as a short column of small squares printed with example weights (0.1, 0.8, …, 0.02) between the keys and the values, braced together into the output, so the reader sees the weighting rather than reads about it.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF's first page (CIKM '19). elements 'other' = the numbered attention-weight squares.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: CTR prediction via self-attentive feature interaction

core.what: one query card (peach, bottom) is braced against a stack of key cards (grey, middle) to give a column of attention weights alpha drawn with example values, which is braced with the value cards (gold, top) into the single output card at the right

relations.form: a curly brace gathers the grey key stack and the peach query card into a dark-gold column of weight cells printed 0.1, 0.8, ..., 0.02
a second, tall curly brace gathers the gold value stack and the weight column into the grey output card e~_m^(h) at the far right

blue projection arrows run left to right from the blue feature-embedding stack e_M to the value stack (straight, top) and key stack (diagonal down), and from the single embedding e_m at bottom left up to the query card, each labelled W_Value / W_Key / W_Query

channels.colour: fill = role of the representation: blue raw embeddings, gold values, grey keys, peach query, dark gold attention weights; the output is a darker grey that echoes the keys without meaning to
channels.shape: flat rectangles stacked like cards with elision dots = sets of field embeddings; small square cells with numbers = attention weights; curly braces = combination operations
channels.line: blue arrows = learned projections, each labelled with its matrix; braces replace lines for the attention and weighted-sum steps

quality.strengths: the attention weights are drawn as data - a column of cells with example values - between the keys and the values, so the compared representations and the result of comparing them are all visible; each projection role has its own fill
quality.weaknesses: the two curly braces stand in for different operations (dot-product scoring and weighted sum) without naming either; the cards are scattered diagonally rather than aligned, so the query's long diagonal arrow and the key arrow cross the figure; the output's grey nearly matches the key cards

insights.structure: One attention head drawn as a scatter: stacked blue feature-embedding cards e_M at top left, a single query embedding e_m at bottom left, projected into gold value cards (top right), grey key cards (middle) and a peach query card, which combine via curly braces into the output e~_m^(h) at right.
insights.data: Embeddings are flat coloured rectangles stacked like cards with dots for elision, and attention weights alpha are a vertical column of dark-gold cells with sample values 0.1, 0.8, ..., 0.02.
insights.emphasis: Each projection role has its own fill colour (gold value, grey key, peach query) and the projection matrices W^(h) are italic labels on the blue arrows.
insights.flow: Left-to-right with blue diagonal arrows for projections, then curly braces gather keys with query into alpha and alpha with values into the output.
insights.avoid: Curly braces stand in for operations (dot product, weighted sum) without naming them, and the diagonal arrow layout scatters the elements loosely.

arrangement.units: unenclosed flat coloured cards and a weight column, no containers
arrangement.inputs_as: stacked blue embedding cards e_M and a single e_m
arrangement.shared: the same e_M stack is projected to both keys and values
